newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada housing starts seen rising further in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Canada housing starts seen rising further in 1997.

text.p: Canadian residential housing starts are estimated to increase by 9.0 percent next year, while renovation spending will rise 5.6 percent, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said in a report released on Thursday.

In its fourth quarter National Housing Outlook, the CMHC said total housing starts were expected to reach 134,600 units in 1997, compared with the 123,400 units projected for this year. The corporation said the single-family housing sector would continue to expand while the multiple-unit sector would rebound from its 1996 decline.

"The upturn in housing activity will be due to a combination of factors," said Alie Manouchehri, senior economist at the CMHC market analysis center. "Projected job creation in 1997 will accompany low mortgage rates and lift both the resale and the new home markets further."
Manouchehri said he expected stable or slightly higher prices in the housing resale market with higher sales volumes.
All Canadian provinces were forecast to record higher housing starts activity this year, with Ontario and Saskatchewan leading the way.
"Construction will accelerate further in 1997 with the larger percentage gains in Alberta and Quebec as a result of a much healthier multiples market," the CMHC said.
Housing starts in Ontario were projected to rise 9.0 percent in 1997, coming close to their 1994 level.

All other provinces, except Newfoundland, Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia, would also record higher starts in 1997. Housing starts in Saskatchewan were also expected to slow down from their high pace this year.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
